newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--resist U.S. Treasuries' slip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--resist U.S. Treasuries' slip.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds might have been bid an eighth of a point lower Monday but offers stayed around unchanged, largely resisting slipping downhill with Treasury bonds, which eased ahead of retail sales data.

"It was inactive, there was not that much selling pressure from institutions or the Street. But the retail (sector) still has been somewhat active, they're buying some bonds," a muncipal bond trader said.

Higher-yielding municipal issues, like hospital and housing bonds, appeared to be drawing individual investors, who seemed to be getting over their initial reluctance to buy at higher price levels achieved over the past few weeks.

While few new issues were sold, traders said a big life and casualty company was spotted buying long-term Texas paper in a $13.885 million sale by Temple Independent School District. The bonds, with maturities from 2012 to 2017, were not re-offered by Coastal Securities.
Traders speculated that unless the Treasury market continues to erode, municipal bond prices should remain fairly strong, as the lack of supply keeps working in their favor.

The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, an indicator of secondary market supplies slipped to $944.3 million, a lean level, which shows Wall Street financial firms have cleaned some bonds off their shelves.

Despite the drop in yields seen over the past few weeks, the summer doldrums appeared to be dampening new offerings, as this week's calender only added up to around $2.507 billion in 122 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings, which totaled $1.780 billion in 47 sales, included a $350 million Los Angeles Unified School District offering through BancAmerica.
On Tuesday, fixed-income traders were looking ahead to retail sales for June, which were forcast at up 0.2 percent, according to a consensus poll of Reuters economists.
And on Wednesday, Consumer Prices for June were due out, also predicted to rise 0.2 percent.
September municipal bond traded on the Chicago Board of Trade ended down four ticks at 119-12/32, while September Treasury bonds shed eased six ticks to 113-30/32. The MOB spread steadied at 174.
In the secondary market, Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania & New Jersey Revenues, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 100, down one eighth.
And Jefferson County, Alabama Sewer Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 102, against 5.50 percent, NET, on Friday.
